findings.condition: The only copper path from C1 pad 2 (GND) to J1 pad 3 (GND) is: 0.25 mm F.Cu track -> one 0.6/0.3 mm via -> B.Cu GND pour -> four thermal spokes (~0.4-0.5 mm effective width each, verified by point-in-polygon sampling of the saved filled_polygon) into J1 pad 3. There is no redundant via or direct F.Cu GND route.

findings.mechanism: A single via barrel or a thermally relieved spoke set is a single point of failure for the ground return: a drill defect, barrel crack, or spoke neck damage opens the filter's shunt path, leaving pin 2 unfiltered (output follows input through R1 with no C1 return). Connectivity as saved is verified good; this is a robustness observation only.
findings.reasoning: The stated exercise criterion is connectivity only, and requirements.txt forbids imposing unstated ratings, so this is not a defect: the saved fill demonstrably connects (verified both by KiCad connectivity rebuild and by my own geometry script against the raw filled_polygon). Reported as info-level concern because the ground net's dependence on a single small via plus thermal spokes is the one physically fragile element of an otherwise fully verified layout, and it is invisible to ERC/DRC pass/fail output.
findings.title: GND return between C1 and J1.3 is a single-path chain through one 0.3 mm-drill via and zone thermal spokes

limitations: Zone fill evaluated as saved; the read-only candidate forbids a refill pass. Mitigated by direct geometric verification of the saved filled polygon rather than relying on tool exit codes.
No fabrication-output (Gerber/drill) generation or soldermask/paste review was performed; not part of the stated criteria.
No current/thermal qualification or component tolerance analysis performed: requirements.txt explicitly forbids imposing unstated ratings, and no load/current figures are declared for the contract.

The wxWidgets PROPERTY_ENUM assert messages in work/geometry/console.log are pcbnew Python-binding noise (exit 0, complete data); I reproduced similar harmless stderr noise locally and treated them as non-findings.
ngspice simulation uses ideal R/C values from the schematic (10k/100n); no parasitics or connector models were included.
